Subject: Prostate MRI | Facility: Amsterdam UMC (AMC) | Date: 10 Jan 2025

Clinical context: Re-evaluation after prior prostate cancer diagnosis. Current PSA 4.4 ng/mL, PI-RADS 5.

FINDINGS:
The gland occupies 91.11 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a focal hypointense area within the left peripheral zone at the base and mid sections, spanning roughly 28 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows marked restriction paired with depressed ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced series reveal early, localized enhancement against the background parenchyma. Capsular integrity remains intact with no seminal vesicle involvement. Pelvic lymph nodes and the bladder appear normal.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone measuring approximately 28 mm. Prostate volume 91.11 mL yielding a PSA density of 0.048 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.78277797.

previous_notes.author: Dr. H. Martens (GP)
previous_notes.text: A scheduled visit addressed the established prostate cancer diagnosis alongside continuous PSA tracking. The initial biopsy yielded ISUP GG 2 results, prompting a second sampling after PSA climbed to 4.0 ng/mL during March 2024. Urology outpatient scheduling facilitated a thorough review of the updated histology. The patient's preference for adaptable booking windows was documented.

previous_notes.author: Dr. H. Martens (GP)
previous_notes.text: Tracking the upward PSA trajectory, which reached 4.0 ng/mL after an initial 3.1 ng/mL reading in May 2023, prompted a urology referral for a second biopsy. The individual reports zero urinary obstruction symptoms and maintains a consistent hiking schedule. Previous positive histology informed the referral pathway. Follow-up imaging and biopsy outcomes were slated for discussion during the subsequent appointment.
